page: Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g is a general-purpose server instance from the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware constraint is the local storage, which is limited to a 1 GB NVMe SSD, necessitating external storage solutions for most data-intensive applications. The instance also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and has no GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top tier. Text processing and small-model LLM text generation also reach top-tier performance levels. However, multi-core operations, including stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, fall into the average range. Memory performance is strong, with the PassMark memory score placing in the top 25%, while uncached memory read and write bandwidths remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores and 64 GB of RAM offer a solid resource density for general-purpose workloads, though the extremely small 1 GB local NVMe SSD represents a significant tradeoff that requires off-instance storage. This server is well-suited for workloads such as text processing, web serving, software compilation, and lightweight LLM inference tasks that do not require substantial local disk space.
